summary: Built hubreg, a stdlib-only Python package where one validated record per action drives the binder, the diagnoser, the assistant's tool schemas, the app's argument controls, help/reference text, the confirmation gate and a walker test, with four demo plug-ins (thermostat.set_temperature, light.dim, door.lock_door, scene.run_scene) and a `python3 -m hubreg describe|call|help|walk` CLI. Binding refuses unknown actions/options before missing arguments, never coerces a type or falls back to a default silently, treats hard limits as refusals and usual ranges as RANGE warnings on supplied values only, and only ever offers redirects as a fix. 154 unittest tests cover registration rules, binding, confirmation, every consumer, the walker's generated probes, the demo shapes, the CLI and the pluggable type table, and the final run is green.

pattern_mapping.Operation record: hubreg/record.py: OpRecord + build_record (name, on, doc, args, fields, samples, run, flags, redirects, validate)
pattern_mapping.Argument spec: hubreg/spec.py: ArgSpec + build_spec (name, type, unit, doc, default/optional, min/max, usual/usual_hint, values, redirects)
pattern_mapping.Argument type: hubreg/argtypes.py: ArgType with keys/accepts/check/example/parse/describe and the number/string/enum/bool types in a per-registry table (Registry.types)
pattern_mapping.Binder: hubreg/binder.py: bind() returns Call or Failure; Registry.bind hands a Failure to the diagnoser and raises the Refusal
pattern_mapping.Diagnoser: hubreg/diagnoser.py: explain(Failure) -> Refusal with valid, nearest, fix, and render_call for fixes
pattern_mapping.Walker: hubreg/walker.py: walk() calls every sample and generates missing-argument, unknown-option, wrong-type, limit, usual-range, redirect and confirmation probes, applying Registry.check_result
pattern_mapping.Flags: record flags.confirm plus host policy in Registry(confirm_required=...), combined by Registry.needs_confirm, asked by run, help, context line and tool schema
pattern_mapping.Cross-argument hook: record key 'validate', normalised by binder._hook_failure into the diagnoser's HOOK vocabulary
pattern_mapping.Redirects: ArgSpec.redirects (option near-misses) and OpRecord.redirects (action near-misses), validated at record build and at finalize, offered only as Refusal.fix
pattern_mapping.Non-record exceptions: hubreg/nonrecord.py: CLI_VERBS and NON_RECORD_ENTRY_POINTS, checked by tests/test_nonrecord.py
pattern_mapping.Demo plug-ins / CLI: hubreg/demo.py: demo_registry(); hubreg/__main__.py: describe, call, help, walk

notes_applied: Note 1: register() validates structure (run present and callable, fields, samples, unique typed args, type-allowed spec keys) and semantics (default passes its type check and the limits, usual range inside the limits, unique (on, name)); finalize() checks what spans records, namely every redirect target, and any RecordError carries code E_BAD_RECORD with the narrower reason in .detail.

Note 2: hard limits are refusals while usual ranges only warn, both in the declared unit; only supplied values warn, a default outside the usual range is silent and documented in help; unknown keys are refused before missing arguments so a near-miss like temp-for-target gets its repair (test_binding.test_unknown_option_is_reported_before_a_missing_argument).

Note 3: unknown keys and wrong types are refusals, never a coerced zero or silent default (bool rejects 1 and 'true', number rejects '80', string rejects 42); bind(None) means no arguments, not a wrong type.

Note 4: every near-miss redirect (option-level in ArgSpec, action-level in OpRecord) is only ever rendered into Refusal.fix; the binder never rewrites a call and the walker asserts that probes using the wrong name are refused, not run. Case-only matches are likewise only offered as a fix.

Note 5: samples live in the record, the walker binds and runs every one, applies the single Registry.check_result (exact declared fields), and generates the probes the records imply (missing argument, unknown option, wrong type, min-1/max+1, enum value outside the list, value outside the usual range, every redirect, the confirmation gate) instead of only a happy path.

Note 6: all type-specific behaviour lives in ArgType (keys, accepts, check, example, parse, describe); the binder never switches on a type name, the type table belongs to the Registry instance, and tests/test_types.py shows a plug-in 'even' type in one registry that does not leak into another.
Note 7: records are keyed by (device kind, action name), so the same name on another kind is a different action; no overloading within a kind.

Note 9: the parts that cannot be records (the CLI verbs) are listed in hubreg/nonrecord.py, and tests/test_nonrecord.py checks every usage verb is listed, no registered action shadows one, and no package module outside demo.py names an action.

Note 11: needs_confirm combines host policy and the record flag so a record cannot lower host policy; run refuses with E_CONFIRM (with a fix) and help, the context line and tool schemas all ask the same question; the walker fails a build that tells the assistant a guarded action is safe or lets one run unconfirmed.

Purposes of the other notes: note 8 (defaults are part of identity) is noted as out of scope with no hashing layer here; note 10 (composite operations) is not needed by TASK.md, so only run-implementations are accepted.
tests: 154 tests in 10 unittest modules under tests/ (records 32, binding 31, run/confirmation 14, consumers 18, walker 11, demo 8, cli 15, interface 10, nonrecord 5, types 10); last run: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` -> Ran 154 tests ... OK, and `python3 -m hubreg walk` -> [].
chapter_feedback: Most useful: the explicit bind order in the Sketch (unknown action, then unknown options before missing arguments, then type/limits, then usual warning, then hook) and notes 2-4; following them literally produced refusal messages that already read well.

Most useful structurally: the participant table plus the mermaid diagram made the module split obvious, and 'every arrow out of the registry is a consumer that would otherwise keep its own copy' was the test I kept applying (one test adds a record and checks all five renderings).

The chapter's error vocabulary is only for calls, but it also asks registration to refuse E_BAD_RECORD while its examples show narrower reasons; I resolved this with one code plus .detail, which the chapter does not discuss.

The chapter puts 'every sample binds' in finalize(); in a library whose tool_schemas() may be called on someone else's half-finished plug-in that is harsher than useful, so samples are only structurally required at registration and are checked by the walker. A sentence on that trade-off would help.

The chapter's flags list mentions confirmation only in passing (note 11), yet TASK.md needs it; the hint that host policy may raise a flag and a record cannot lower it was the single most valuable sentence, because the natural implementation (asking the record) gets it wrong.

Ambiguity I had to guess: whether a case-insensitive near-match should populate `fix` or only `nearest`; the Sketch says `fix: r.call or none` for unknown methods, but note 4 says a case-insensitive match is 'offered as the fix'. I set fix only for declared redirects and for case-only differences.

Missing from the chapter: guidance on what a tool schema should look like when an action has a usual range (I used x-unit/x-usual/description), and on how to render a result when the record declares fields rather than a result kind (I render {field, field}).
The warning about the walker 'proving less than it seems' was accurate and immediately useful: my first walker let an implementation that raises escape entirely, which the chapter predicted.
